newsitem.title: JAPAN: Four more ex-DKB executives indicted-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Four more ex-DKB executives indicted-Jiji.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors have indicted four more former executives of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd on charges of violating Japan's Commercial Code by approving illegal loans to a corporate racketeer, Jiji news agency reported on Monday.

Prosecutors charged that the four men conspired to provide loans of about 8.8 billion yen to Ryuichi Koike, a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer at the heart of a scandal which has already ensnared Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Sokaiya extort money from corporations by threatening to disrupt their annual shareholders meetings.
Four other DKB officials have already been indicted in connection with the scandal.
The latest to be indicted are former DKB vice presidents Akira Kanazawa, and Tsuneo Uchida, former senior managing director Yasuyuki Terasawa, and former managing director Kenji Tanaka, Jiji said.
Tanaka was president of the major supermarket chain Jusco Co Ltd at the time of his arrest.
The four were arrested in June.
Prosecutors are continuing to investigate the possible involvement of former DKB chairman Tadashi Okuda in the scandal, Jiji said.
